title: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany Scholarship)
official_source: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF/BMFTR) + Private Sponsors
program_type: Public-private partnership scholarship (Federal Government + private sponsors, administered by universities)
duration: Minimum 2 semesters, renewable up to standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit)
description: The Deutschlandstipendium is funded by the German Foreign Office with around 900 scholarships for excellent international students each year. It pays EUR 300 per month for 12 months, extendable to 24 months for master's students, plus insurance contributions. Applications are made directly to the university, which publishes its own application period, forms and subject-specific criteria, and either selects the scholars itself or forwards candidates for the DAI to decide. Eligibility requires being admitted to a German university and migrating to Germany to study.

title: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship
degree: Undergraduate, Graduate, Japanese Language Institute, College of Technology, Specialized Training College
program_type: Government scholarship for privately-financed international students (Japan Student Services Organization - JASSO)
duration: 12 months (April to March) or 6 months (October to March)
description: The Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a JASSO programme for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are already enrolled at a Japanese educational institution and are facing financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of 48,000 yen at graduate or undergraduate level and 30,000 yen at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months from April or 6 months from October. Applications are made through the enrolled institution rather than directly to JASSO, so timing and eligibility are institution

title: POSCO TJ Park Foundation Global Scholarship
program_type: Private-sector foundation scholarship (POSCO Group) administered by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation
duration: Master's: 4 semesters of tuition support and 22 months of living expenses. Doctoral or integrated master's and doctoral: 6 semesters of tuition support and 36 months of living expenses.
description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea is the inbound component of the POSCO Global Scholarship operated by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation, and it is described by the Foundation as 'The Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program'. It funds non-Korean nationals admitted to Master's or doctoral programmes at designated Korean graduate schools, who must be recommended by their admitting institution. title: ETH Zurich Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP)
official_source: ETH Zurich and ETH Zurich Foundation
duration: Regular duration of the Master's programme (three or four semesters)
description: ETH Zurich's ESOP supports excellent Master's students with a scholarship, mentorship and a network of the ETH Foundation. The page states that the scholarship covers the full study and living costs during the Master's degree course, and that the award consists of a scholarship covering living and study expenses of CHF 12'000 per semester (13'500 CHF per semester from HS27 onwards) plus a tuition fee waiver. The scholarship and the waiver are both awarded for the regular duration of the Master's programme (three or four semesters). Approximately 60 ESOP scholarships are assigned for the 2027/2

title: EPFL Master Excellence Fellowships
program_type: University excellence fellowship funded by philanthropy (Student Support Program, 'Attract Talent' pillar)
duration: Master's programme, renewable for a second year subject to 50 ECTS credits and a 5.0/6 average
description: EPFL offers a limited number of Master Excellence Fellowships to reward outstanding students beginning their Master's studies at the school, combining a financial award with guaranteed housing. Each fellowship is worth CHF 10,000 per semester and is open both to EPFL Bachelor's graduates and to students who began their university studies elsewhere. Selection weighs remarkable academic results together with extracurricular achievements in research, entrepreneurship, sport, arts or civic activity. title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships
program_type: EU research grant / research fellowship under Horizon Europe, administered by the European Research Executive Agency
duration: European Postdoctoral Fellowships: 12 to 24 months. Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: an outgoing phase of 12 to 24 months in a non-associated Third Country plus a mandatory 12-month return phase in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
description: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers. There are two types: European Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting 12 to 24 months in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and open to any nationality; and Global Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting an outgoing phase of 12 to 24 months in a non-associated Third Country followed by a mandatory 12-month return phase, open only to nationals or long-term residents of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countrie

title: Erasmus+ Student Exchange (Studying Abroad)
program_type: EU exchange and mobility programme (Erasmus+ Key Action 1), funded by the European Commission
duration: Long-term mobility: minimum 2 months to maximum 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days abroad, which must be blended mobilities; only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. Maximum total duration is 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.
description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs
